path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-105. Exempt controlled substances, other drugs, devices and cosmetics
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-105. Exempt controlled substances, other drugs, devices and cosmetics
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-105. Exempt controlled substances, other drugs, devices and cosmetics (2023)
content:
Except as set forth in the Schedules of Controlled Substances ofsection 4of this act1or otherwise provided herein, the secretary, after consultation with and upon the
   recommendation of the board, may, by regulation, exempt from the provisions of this
   act relating to controlled substances, other drugs, devices and cosmetics to such
   extent as he determines to be consistent with the public health.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-110. New drugs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-110. New drugs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-110. New drugs (2023)
content:
No person shall sell, deliver, offer for sale, hold for sale, or give away, any new
   drug unless (i) an application with respect thereto has been approved or a notice
   of claimed investigational exemption for a new drug has been filed under the appropriate
   Federal act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.3. Methamphetamine production
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.3. Methamphetamine production
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.3. Methamphetamine production (2023)
content:
(a) Proof that a person had in his possession more than 40 grams or 15 packages of
      any drug containing ephedrine, pseudoephedrine or phenylpropanolamine, or any of their
      salts, optical isomers or salts of optical isomers as an active ingredient shall give
      rise to a rebuttable presumption that the person acted with intent to manufacture
      methamphetamine.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-117. Probation without verdict
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-117. Probation without verdict
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-117. Probation without verdict (2023)
content:
Except as provided in clause (1) of this subsection, the court may place a person
   on probation without verdict if the person pleads nolo contendere or guilty to any
   nonviolent offense under this act and the person proves he is drug dependent.  For the purposes of proving drug dependency, the person must present the testimony
   of a physician or psychologist trained in the field of drug abuse.  The term of probation shall be for a specific time period not to exceed the maximum
   for the offense upon such reasonable terms and conditions as the court may require.  The following shall apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.5. Environmental costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.5. Environmental costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.5. Environmental costs (2023)
content:
In addition to restitution under18 Pa.C.S. § 1110(relating to restitution for cleanup of clandestine laboratories), a person who is
   convicted of an offense involving the operation of a methamphetamine laboratory or
   the possession or use of a precursor or reagent substance to manufacture methamphetamine
   shall be ordered to reimburse the appropriate law enforcement agency, emergency medical
   services organization, fire company or other organization for the costs of cleaning
   up the environmental hazards associated with the operation of the laboratory or the
   possession or use of a precursor or reagent substance to manufacture methamphetamine.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.9. Secure storage of xylazine
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.9. Secure storage of xylazine
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.9. Secure storage of xylazine (2023)
content:
A practitioner who is a veterinarian shall comply with the provisions of section 4(a)(5)
   of the act of September 27, 1961 (P.L. 1700, No. 699),1known as the “Pharmacy Act,” for the storage and protection of xylazine.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.8. Drug overdose medication

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-113.8. Drug overdose medication (2023)
content: (a) The department, in carrying out its duties under28 Pa. Code Ch. 1023(relating to personnel),1shall have the following duties:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-115. Second or subsequent offense
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-115. Second or subsequent offense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-115. Second or subsequent offense (2023)
content:
(a) Any person convicted of a second or subsequent offense under clause (30) of subsection
      (a) of section 13 of this act1or of a similar offense under any statute of the United States or of any state may
      be imprisoned for a term up to twice the term otherwise authorized, fined an amount
      up to twice that otherwise authorized, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-118. Disposition in lieu of trial or criminal punishment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-118. Disposition in lieu of trial or criminal punishment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-118. Disposition in lieu of trial or criminal punishment (2023)
content:
(a) If a person charged with a nonviolent crime claims to be drug dependent or a drug
      abuser and prior to trial he requests appropriate treatment, including but not limited
      to, admission or commitment under the Mental Health and Mental Retardation Act of
      19661in lieu of criminal prosecution, a physician experienced or trained in the field
      of drug dependency or drug abuse shall be appointed by the court to examine, if necessary,
      and to review the accused's record and advise the government attorney, the accused
      and the court in writing setting forth that for the treatment and rehabilitation of
      the accused it would be preferable for the criminal charges to be held in abeyance
      or withdrawn in order to institute treatment for drug dependence, or for the criminal
      charges to be prosecuted.  The government attorney shall exercise his discretion whether or not to accept the
      physician's recommendation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-119. Expunging criminal records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-119. Expunging criminal records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-119. Expunging criminal records (2023)
content:
(a) Any records of arrest or prosecution or both for a criminal offense under this
      act, except for persons indicted for violations of clause (30) of subsection (a) of
      section 13,1or under the provisions previously governing controlled substances in the Commonwealth
      of Pennsylvania or any political subdivision thereof shall be promptly expunged from
      the official and unofficial arrest and other criminal records pertaining to that individual
      when the charges are withdrawn or dismissed or the person is acquitted of the charges:
      Provided, That such expungement shall be available as a matter of right to any person
      only once.  Within five days after such withdrawal, dismissal or acquittal the court, in writing,
      shall order the appropriate keepers of criminal records (i) to expunge and destroy
      the official and unofficial arrest and other criminal records of that individual,
      to request in so far as they are able the return of such records as they have made
      available to Federal and other State agencies, and to destroy such records on receipt
      thereof;  and (ii) to file with the court within thirty days an affidavit that such
      records have been expunged and destroyed, together with the court's expunction order
      and to retain no copies thereof.  Upon receipt of such affidavit, the court shall seal the same together with the
      original and all copies of its expunction order and shall not permit any person or
      agency to examine such sealed documents.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-114. Distribution to persons under age eighteen
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-114. Distribution to persons under age eighteen
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-114. Distribution to persons under age eighteen (2023)
content:
Any person who is at least twenty-one years of age and who is not himself a drug dependent
   person who violates this act by distributing a controlled substance listed in Schedules
   I through V1to a person under eighteen years of age who is at least four years his junior is
   punishable by a term of imprisonment up to twice that otherwise authorized by subsection
   (f) of section 13 of this act,2in addition to any fine authorized by this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-120. Offenses by a corporation, copartnership or association
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-120. Offenses by a corporation, copartnership or association
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-120. Offenses by a corporation, copartnership or association (2023)
content:
If any violation of the provisions of this act is by a corporation, copartnership
   or association, the officers and directors of such corporation or the members of such
   copartnership or association, the agents and employes with prior guilty knowledge
   of the fact, shall be deemed guilty of a violation of the provisions of this act to
   the same extent as though said violation were committed by them personally.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-122. Judicial review
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-122. Judicial review
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-122. Judicial review (2023)
content:
Any person aggrieved by a final administrative decision may obtain review of the decision
   pursuant to the provisions of the Administrative Agency Law.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-124. Administrative inspections and warrants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-124. Administrative inspections and warrants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-124. Administrative inspections and warrants (2023)
content: (a) As used in this section, the term“controlled premises”means:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-121. Burden of proving exemptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-121. Burden of proving exemptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-121. Burden of proving exemptions (2023)
content:
In any prosecution under this act, it shall not be necessary to negate any of the
   exemptions or exceptions of this act in any complaint, information or trial.  The burden of proof of such exemption or exception shall be upon the person claiming
   it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-126. Cooperation with other authorities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-126. Cooperation with other authorities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-126. Cooperation with other authorities (2023)
content:
The agencies charged with the enforcement of this act shall actively cooperate and
   coordinate with the agencies charged with the enforcement of all Federal and State
   laws relating to the regulation of the distribution of controlled substances, other
   drugs, devices or cosmetics.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-123. Revocation of licenses of practitioners
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-123. Revocation of licenses of practitioners
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-123. Revocation of licenses of practitioners (2023)
content:
(a) Any license or registration heretofore issued to any practitioner may either be
      revoked or suspended by the proper officers or boards having power to issue licenses
      or registration to any of the foregoing, upon proof that the licensee or registrant
      is a drug dependent person on the use of any controlled substance, after giving such
      licensee or registrant reasonable notice and opportunity to be heard.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-125. Injunctive relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-125. Injunctive relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-125. Injunctive relief (2023)
content:
In addition to the remedies provided herein, the secretary is hereby authorized to
   apply to the court of common pleas in the county in which such violation occurs or
   to the Commonwealth Court for, and such court shall have jurisdiction to grant, a
   temporary or permanent injunction restraining any person from continued violation
   of any provision of this act irrespective of the existence of an adequate remedy at
   law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-130. Hearing examiners
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-130. Hearing examiners
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-130. Hearing examiners (2023)
content:
(a) The secretary shall appoint, with the approval of the Governor, such hearing examiners
      as shall be necessary to conduct hearings as provided in section 27.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-131. Board creation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-131. Board creation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-131. Board creation (2023)
content:
(a) There is hereby created within the Department of Health a departmental administrative
      board to be known as the “Pennsylvania Drug, Device and Cosmetic Board.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-127. Embargo
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-127. Embargo
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-127. Embargo (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever a duly authorized officer of the secretary finds or has probable cause
      to believe that any controlled substance, other drug, device or cosmetic is adulterated
      or misbranded or contraband, the same shall be deemed subject to embargo and he shall
      affix to such substance or article a tag or other appropriate marking, approved by
      the secretary, giving notice that such substance or article is or is suspected of
      being adulterated, misbranded or contraband and warning all persons not to remove
      or dispose of such substance or article until permission so to do has been granted
      by such officer, or until it shall have determined by proper authority that such substance
      or article is not adulterated, misbranded or contraband.  At the time such notice is offered, the officer shall provide the person in charge
      of such substance or article, if any, or the owner, if he is known, a statement in
      writing, setting forth both the basis for the embargo and supporting facts.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-132. Persons authorized to prescribe drugs to remain as heretofore
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-132. Persons authorized to prescribe drugs to remain as heretofore
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-132. Persons authorized to prescribe drugs to remain as heretofore (2023)
content:
No provision of this act or any rule or regulation promulgated pursuant to this act
   shall authorize or be construed as authorizing any person to prescribe drugs who is
   not specifically so authorized under existing law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-134. Administration of act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-134. Administration of act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-134. Administration of act (2023)
content:
(a) Except as may be otherwise provided by law, the provisions of this act shall be
      administered by the department.  The secretary is authorized to employ personnel and to fix their compensation subject
      to the act of April 9, 1929 (P.L. 177), known as “The Administrative Code of 1929.”1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-133. Conformity with federal law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-133. Conformity with federal law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-133. Conformity with federal law (2023)
content:
No controlled substance, other drug, device or cosmetic shall be deemed to be adulterated
   or misbranded under this act if it complies with the applicable Federal act and/or
   regulations and interpretations issued pursuant thereto, unless the secretary, after
   consultation with and upon the recommendation of the board, shall have previously
   promulgated a regulation stating that the applicable provision of the Federal act
   and/or regulations and interpretations thereof would not be followed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-135. Promulgation of regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-135. Promulgation of regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-135. Promulgation of regulations (2023)
content:
(a) The secretary shall have the authority to promulgate in accordance with the provisions
      of this section and of the act of July 31, 1968 (P.L. 769, No. 240), known as the
      “Commonwealth Documents Law”1any regulations hereinbefore referred to in this act and such other regulations with
      the consent of the board regarding the possession, distribution, sale, purchase or
      manufacture of controlled substances, other drugs or devices or cosmetics as may be
      necessary to aid in the enforcement of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-136. Administrative procedure
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-136. Administrative procedure
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-136. Administrative procedure (2023)
content:
The administrative Agency Law, as amended,1shall be applicable in its entirety to the Department of Health in the administration
   of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-138. Savings provision
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-138. Savings provision
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-138. Savings provision (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act shall not affect any act done, liability incurred, or right
   accrued or vested, or affect any suit or prosecution pending to enforce any right
   or penalty or punish any offense under the authority of any Act of Assembly, or part
   thereof, repealed by this act:  Provided, however, That in any case final on or before
   June 12, 1972 in which a defendant was sentenced for the commission of acts similar
   to those proscribed by subsection (16) or (31), but not (30), of section 13(a) of
   this act, such defendant shall be resentenced under this act upon his petition if
   the penalties hereunder are less than those under prior law and in such case the prior
   criminal record of the defendant shall be expunged to the extent that such record
   shall no longer contain any reference to the prior grade of the offense if higher
   than the grade of the offense to which defendant is resentenced.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-141.1. Effect on local ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-141.1. Effect on local ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-141.1. Effect on local ordinances (2023)
content:
Nothing in this act relating to drug paraphernalia shall be deemed to supersede or
   invalidate any consistent local ordinance, including zoning and nuisance ordinances,
   relating to the possession, sale or use of drug paraphernalia.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-139. Pending proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-139. Pending proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-139. Pending proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) Prosecution for any violation of law occurring prior to the effective date of
      this act is not affected or abated by this act.  In any case not yet final if the offense is similar to one set out in this act,
      the penalties under this act apply if they are less than those under prior law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-137. Cooperative agreements and confidentiality
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-137. Cooperative agreements and confidentiality
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-137. Cooperative agreements and confidentiality (2023)
content:
(a) The secretary shall cooperate with Federal and other State agencies in discharging
      his responsibilities concerning traffic in controlled substances, other drugs, devices
      and cosmetics and in suppressing the abuse of such substances and articles.  To this end, he may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-140. Continuation of regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-140. Continuation of regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-140. Continuation of regulations (2023)
content:
Any orders and regulations promulgated under any law affected by this act and in effect
   on the effective date of this act and not in conflict with it continue in effect until
   modified, superseded or repealed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-142. Bar to prosecution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-142. Bar to prosecution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-142. Bar to prosecution (2023)
content:
If a violation of this act is a violation of a Federal law or the law of another state,
   a conviction or acquittal under Federal law or the law of another state for the same
   act is a bar to prosecution in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-141. Uniformity of interpretation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-141. Uniformity of interpretation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-141. Uniformity of interpretation (2023)
content:
This act shall be so applied and construed as to effectuate its general purpose to
   make uniform the law with respect to the subject of this act among those states which
   enact similar legislation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-151. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-151. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-151. Short title (2023)
content:
This act shall be known and may be cited as the Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers
   Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-144. Effective dates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-144. Effective dates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-144. Effective dates (2023)
content: Sections 13, 14, 15, 20 and 391shall take effect immediately.  All other sections shall take effect on June 14, 1972.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-143. Repeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6. The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-143. Repeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-143. Repeals (2023)
content:
(a) The act of September 26, 1961 (P.L. 1664), known as “The Drug, Device and Cosmetic
      Act,”1is hereby repealed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-153. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-153. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-153. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this act shall have the meanings given
   to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-154. Nature of actions and jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-154. Nature of actions and jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-154. Nature of actions and jurisdiction (2023)
content:
The causes of action established in this act are civil actions to evict or remove
   tenants or other persons from leased residential premises.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-155. Standing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-155. Standing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-155. Standing (2023)
content: A civil action under this act may be brought by any of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-152. Legislative findings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-152. Legislative findings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-152. Legislative findings (2023)
content: The General Assembly finds and declares as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-158. Mandatory partial eviction where affirmative defense or exemption to complete eviction is established
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-158. Mandatory partial eviction where affirmative defense or exemption to complete eviction is established
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-158. Mandatory partial eviction where affirmative defense or exemption to complete eviction is established (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If the plaintiff has established grounds for a complete eviction but the court finds
      that the tenant has satisfactorily established the basis for an affirmative defense
      or exemption under section 7 and if the court elects not to order the complete eviction
      of the tenant, the court, except as otherwise provided in section 25, shall order
      the immediate removal from the leased residential premises of any person other than
      the tenant, including adult or minor members of the tenant's household, who have engaged
      in drug-related criminal activity on any portion of the leased residential premises.  Persons removed under this section shall be permanently barred from returning to
      or reentering any portion of the leased residential premises.  The court shall further order as an express condition of the tenancy that the tenant
      shall not give permission to or invite any person who has been removed under this
      act to return to or reenter any portion of the leased residential premises.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-156. Remedies and judicial orders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-156. Remedies and judicial orders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-156. Remedies and judicial orders (2023)
content:
(a) Grounds for complete eviction.--Subject to the provisions of sections 7 and 25, the court shall order the immediate
      eviction, as set forth in sections 12(b) and 14, of a tenant if it finds any of the
      following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-157. Affirmative defense or exemption to a complete eviction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-157. Affirmative defense or exemption to a complete eviction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-157. Affirmative defense or exemption to a complete eviction (2023)
content:
(a) Affirmative defense.--The court may refrain from ordering the complete eviction of a tenant under section
      6(a), if the tenant has established that the tenant was not involved in the drug-related
      criminal activity and that the tenant:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-164. Expedited proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-164. Expedited proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-164. Expedited proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) Expedited hearing.--If a complaint is filed initiating an action under this act, the court shall set the
      matter for a hearing which shall be held on an expedited basis and within 15 days
      following the filing of the complaint.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-159. Substitution of plaintiff
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-159. Substitution of plaintiff
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-159. Substitution of plaintiff (2023)
content:
If the court determines in its discretion that the plaintiff bringing an action under
   this act has failed to prosecute the matter with reasonable diligence, the court may
   substitute as plaintiff any person that consents and that would have been authorized
   under this act to initiate the action.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-166. Inapplicability of exclusionary rule
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-166. Inapplicability of exclusionary rule
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-166. Inapplicability of exclusionary rule (2023)
content:
No relevant testimony or evidence shall be excluded from any civil action brought
   under this act on account of the manner by which it was obtained by a law enforcement
   officer or agency, notwithstanding that the civil action may have been brought by
   a district attorney or the Attorney General.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-163. Impermissible defense
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-163. Impermissible defense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-163. Impermissible defense (2023)
content:
It shall not be a defense to an action brought under this act that the drug-related
   criminal activity was an isolated incident or otherwise has not recurred or that the
   person who actually engaged in the drug-related criminal activity no longer resides
   in the tenant's individual rental unit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-165. Notice to interested parties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-165. Notice to interested parties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-165. Notice to interested parties (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other provision of law concerning the procedures otherwise used
   in eviction proceedings, it shall not be necessary to provide notice to the tenant
   to vacate the premises prior to filing the complaint initiating a civil action under
   this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-160. Execution of removal or eviction order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-160. Execution of removal or eviction order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-160. Execution of removal or eviction order (2023)
content:
Any removal or eviction order issued by a court under this act shall be enforced by
   the person or entity bringing the action.  The appropriate law enforcement agency shall upon the request of the person bringing
   the action assume responsibility for the actual execution of the removal or eviction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-161. Obstructing the execution or enforcement of a removal or eviction order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-161. Obstructing the execution or enforcement of a removal or eviction order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-161. Obstructing the execution or enforcement of a removal or eviction order (2023)
content:
Any person who knowingly violates any order issued under this act or who knowingly
   interferes with, obstructs, impairs or prevents any law enforcement officer from enforcing
   or executing any order issued under this act shall be subject to criminal contempt.  Nothing in this section shall be construed in any way to preclude or preempt a criminal
   prosecution for any other criminal offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-162. Motion to enforce removal order and mandatory evictions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-162. Motion to enforce removal order and mandatory evictions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-162. Motion to enforce removal order and mandatory evictions (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any person authorized to bring an action under this act may move to enforce a removal
      order issued under this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-169. Protection of threatened witnesses or affiants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-169. Protection of threatened witnesses or affiants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-169. Protection of threatened witnesses or affiants (2023)
content:
If proof necessary to establish the grounds for eviction depends, in whole or in part,
   upon the affidavits or testimony of witnesses who are not peace officers, the court
   may upon a showing of prior threats of violence or acts of violence by any defendant
   or any other person issue orders to protect those witnesses, including, but not limited
   to, the nondisclosure of the name, address or any other information which may identify
   those witnesses.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-167. Relation to criminal proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-167. Relation to criminal proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-167. Relation to criminal proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) Criminal proceedings, conviction or adjudications not required.--The fact that a criminal prosecution involving the drug-related criminal activity
      is not commenced or, if commenced, has not yet been concluded or has terminated without
      a conviction or adjudication of delinquency shall not preclude a civil action or the
      issuance of an order under this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-171. Recovery of costs by prevailing plaintiff
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-171. Recovery of costs by prevailing plaintiff
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-171. Recovery of costs by prevailing plaintiff (2023)
content:
A tenant organization or district attorney or the Attorney General bringing a successful
   action under this act, including where the action is ultimately discharged under section
   25(k), shall be entitled to recover the cost of the suit, including reasonable attorney
   fees from the landlord, if the landlord had refused to initiate an action within ten
   days after having been requested to do so in writing, delivered personally or by certified
   mail, return receipt requested.  If the court determines under section 9 that a landlord failed to prosecute an initiated
   action with reasonable diligence, the landlord shall be responsible for the payment
   of all reasonable costs of the suit expended by a prevailing substitute plaintiff
   designated under section 9.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-173. Cumulative remedies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-173. Cumulative remedies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-173. Cumulative remedies (2023)
content:
The remedies authorized by this act shall be cumulative with each other and shall
   be in addition to, not in lieu of, any other remedies available at law or in equity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-170. Ongoing collection of rent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-170. Ongoing collection of rent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-170. Ongoing collection of rent (2023)
content:
A landlord shall be entitled to collect rent due and owing from the tenant during
   the pendency of a civil action brought under this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-168. Discovery
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-168. Discovery
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-168. Discovery (2023)
content:
The parties to an action brought under this act shall not be entitled to conduct discovery
   otherwise available in a civil action except by leave of court where required to ensure
   the fair disposition of the civil action.  The plaintiff in a civil action brought under this act must provide to the tenant
   and all other named defendants a reasonable opportunity prior to the hearing to examine
   any relevant documents or records within the plaintiff's possession which directly
   relate to the action.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-174. Civil immunity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-174. Civil immunity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-174. Civil immunity (2023)
content:
A person who in good faith institutes, participates in or encourages a person to institute
   or participate in a civil action brought under this act or who in good faith provides
   information relied upon by any person in instituting or participating in a civil action
   under this act shall have immunity from civil liability that might otherwise be incurred
   or imposed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-172. Preliminary or emergency relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-172. Preliminary or emergency relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-172. Preliminary or emergency relief (2023)
content:
The court may issue a temporary restraining order, grant preliminary relief or take
   such other action necessary to enjoin or prevent the commission of drug-related criminal
   activity on or in the immediate vicinity of leased residential premises or otherwise
   to protect the rights and interests of all tenants and residents.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-175. Probationary tenancy

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Adulteration or Misbranding › PA ST 35 P.S. § 781. Adulterated drugs; sale prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 781. Adulterated drugs; sale prohibited (2023)
content:
No person shall, within this State, manufacture for sale, offer for sale or sell,
   any drug which is adulterated within the meaning of this act.  The termdrugused herein shall include any medicinal substance or any preparation authorized or
   known in the “Pharmacopoeia of the United States,” or the “National Formulary,” or
   the American Homeopathic Pharmacopoeia, or the American Homeopathic Dispensatory.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Physician's Name on Prescription Form › PA ST 35 P.S. § 806.1. Physician's name printed or stamped on prescription form

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-178. Liberal construction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6A. Expedited Eviction of Drug Traffickers Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 780-178. Liberal construction

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Anabolic Steroids›PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.4. Violations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Anabolic Steroids › PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.4. Violations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.4. Violations (2023)
content:
No physician, or other person regulated by the act of December 20, 1985 (P.L. 457,
   No. 112), known as the Medical Practice Act of 1985,1shall dispense, inject or prescribe an anabolic steroid for the purpose of hormonal
   manipulation intended to increase muscle mass, strength, weight without a medical
   necessity to do so, or for the intended purpose of improving performance in any form
   of exercise, sport or game.  The State Board of Medicine shall promulgate guidelines providing specific periods
   of license suspension or revocation for dispensing, injecting or prescribing anabolic
   steroids in violation of this section.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Anabolic Steroids › PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.3. Penalties

      any pupil found in violation of the rules and regulations required under section 1:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Anabolic Steroids›PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.5. Prescriptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Anabolic Steroids › PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.5. Prescriptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.5. Prescriptions (2023)

Any prescription for an anabolic steroid written in this Commonwealth shall state

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Anabolic Steroids›PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.2. Education regarding steroid use
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Anabolic Steroids › PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.2. Education regarding steroid use
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.2. Education regarding steroid use (2023)
content:
The board of school directors in every school district shall include education regarding
   the dangers of anabolic steroids with any other drug and alcohol program required
   by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated›PA ST 35 P.S. § 821. Sale, etc., of cocaine and eucaine
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated › PA ST 35 P.S. § 821. Sale, etc., of cocaine and eucaine
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 821. Sale, etc., of cocaine and eucaine (2023)
content:
No person shall sell, furnish, or give away cocaine, or its salts, derivatives or
   compounds;  or alpha or beta eucaine, or their salts, derivatives or compounds;  or
   any substance or preparation containing cocaine, its salts, derivatives, or compounds,
   or alpha or beta eucaine, their salts, derivatives, or compounds, except upon the
   prescription of a duly registered, practicing physician, or of a dentist, or of a
   veterinarian, which prescription shall be filled but once, and of which no copy shall
   be taken by any one, and which shall be retained and kept on file by the dispenser
   thereof for a period of at least five years;  nor shall any physician, dentist, or
   veterinarian prescribe, sell, or give away any cocaine, or its salts, derivatives,
   or compounds, or any alpha or beta eucaine or their salts, derivatives, or compounds,
   to any person known to such physician, dentist, or veterinarian to be an habitual
   user of those drugs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Anabolic Steroids›PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.1. School directors to prohibit steroids
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Anabolic Steroids › PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.1. School directors to prohibit steroids
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 807.1. School directors to prohibit steroids (2023)
content:
The board of school directors in every school district in this Commonwealth shall
   prescribe, adopt and enforce rules and regulations to prohibit the use of anabolic
   steroids, except for a valid medical purpose, by any pupil involved in school-related
   athletics.  Body building, muscle enhancement, increasing muscle bulk or strength or the enhancement
   of athletic ability is not a valid medical purpose.  Human Growth Hormone (HGH) shall not be included as an anabolic steroid under the
   provisions of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated›PA ST 35 P.S. § 823. Reports of sales by wholesalers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated › PA ST 35 P.S. § 823. Reports of sales by wholesalers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 823. Reports of sales by wholesalers (2023)
content:
And further, it shall be the duty of all wholesale dealers to make quarterly reports
   of their sales to other dealers, wholesalers or retailers, of cocaine or its salts,
   derivatives, or compounds, or any substance or preparation containing cocaine, its
   salts, derivatives or compounds, alpha or beta eucaine, their salts, derivatives,
   or compounds, to the State Pharmaceutical Examining Board,1upon blanks to be provided for this purpose by the said Board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated›PA ST 35 P.S. § 822. Sales by wholesalers and manufacturers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated › PA ST 35 P.S. § 822. Sales by wholesalers and manufacturers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 822. Sales by wholesalers and manufacturers (2023)
content:
Provided, That the provisions of this act shall not apply to persons engaged in the
   wholesale drug trade, regularly selling cocaine, its salts, derivatives, or compounds,
   or alpha or beta eucaine, their salts, derivatives, or compounds, to persons engaged
   in the retail drug trade, under the following conditions:  That the wholesale dealer
   shall affix or cause to be affixed to the bottle, box, vessel, or package containing
   the article sold, and upon the outside wrapper of the package as originally put up,
   a label distinctly displaying the name and quantity of cocaine or its salts, alpha
   or beta eucaine, or their salts, sold, and the word “poison,” with the name and place
   of business of the seller--all printed in red ink:  And provided also, That the wholesale
   dealer shall, before delivering any of the articles, make or cause to be made, in
   a book kept for the purpose, an entry of the sale thereof, stating the date of sale,
   the quantity, name, and form in which sold, the name and address of the purchaser,
   and the name of the person by whom the entry is made,--and the said book shall be
   always open for inspection by the proper authorities, and shall be preserved for at
   least five years after the date of the last entry made therein:  And provided also,
   That any manufacturer may sell to another manufacturer of the same article or to a
   wholesale dealer in drugs, or a wholesale dealer in drugs may sell to a manufacturer
   of the same article or to another wholesale dealer in drugs, alkaloid cocaine, or
   its salts, derivatives, or compounds, or alpha or beta eucaine, or their salts, derivatives,
   or compounds, or any substance or preparation containing cocaine, its salts, derivatives
   or compounds, alpha or beta eucaine, their salts, derivatives, or compounds, in their
   original package.  Such package shall be labeled as herein provided, and shall be securely sealed.  Each manufacturer and each wholesale dealer in drugs shall, before the delivery
   or at the time of the receipt, as the case may be, of any such drug, enter or cause
   to be entered in a book to be kept by them respectively for that purpose, a record
   of the purchase and sale of such drug, stating the date of purchase and the name and
   address of the person to whom sold, the quantity, name, and form in which sold, and
   a description of the package or container in which sold, and how sealed, and there
   shall also be entered in such book, at the place of such record, a statement that
   such drug was sold or purchased, as the case may be, in the original package, that
   the seals thereon were undamaged and unbroken, and the labels were attached thereto
   as herein provided and were not in any manner defaced or damaged, which statement
   shall be signed by the person selling such drug, in the book herein required to be
   kept by him.  Each manufacturer and each wholesale dealer shall also file, as a part of this record,
   all orders for cocaine, its salts, derivatives, or compounds, or alpha or beta eucaine,
   their salts, derivatives, or compounds;  or any substance or preparation containing
   its salts, derivatives, or compounds;  alpha or beta eucaine, their salts, derivatives,
   or compounds, from other dealers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated›PA ST 35 P.S. § 824. Punishment for violations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated › PA ST 35 P.S. § 824. Punishment for violations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 824. Punishment for violations (2023)
content:
Any person violating any of the provisions of this act shall be sentenced to pay a
   fine of not more than five hundred dollars, and undergo an imprisonment of not more
   than two years, or both, or either, at the discretion of the court.

content: (a) System query.--A prescriber shall query the system:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated›PA ST 35 P.S. § 825. Illegal possession; punishment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated › PA ST 35 P.S. § 825. Illegal possession; punishment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 825. Illegal possession; punishment (2023)
content:
If any person--not being a practicing physician, dentist, or veterinarian, or manufacturer,
   or wholesale or retail dealer in drugs--shall have in his or her possession any cocaine,
   alpha or beta eucaine, or their salts, or any patent or proprietary remedies containing
   the same, except by reason of a prescription of a practicing physician, dentist, or
   veterinarian, he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, be
   sentenced to pay a fine of not more than one hundred dollars, and undergo an imprisonment
   of not more than six months, or both or either, at the discretion of the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated›PA ST 35 P.S. § 826. Enforcement of act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Cocaine, Sale and Possession Regulated › PA ST 35 P.S. § 826. Enforcement of act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 826. Enforcement of act (2023)
content:
The enforcement of this act shall be entrusted to the State Pharmaceutical Examining
   Board, appointed under the act of May twenty-fourth, one thousand eight hundred and
   eighty-seven,1who shall appoint to carry out the provisions of this act an executive secretary,
   and shall also have power to employ such agents, chemists, and assistants as may be
   necessary for this purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Drugs as Evidence›PA ST 35 P.S. § 828. Confiscation of drugs offered in evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Drugs as Evidence › PA ST 35 P.S. § 828. Confiscation of drugs offered in evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 828. Confiscation of drugs offered in evidence (2023)
content:
All drugs offered in evidence in the trial of any cause in this Commonwealth involving
   illegal sale or possession of such drugs, shall be confiscated by the district attorney
   of the county in which said trial takes place.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Forfeiture of Vehicles Transporting Drugs›PA ST 35 P.S. § 831.1. Forfeiture for storage or transportation of narcotics or drugs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Forfeiture of Vehicles Transporting Drugs › PA ST 35 P.S. § 831.1. Forfeiture for storage or transportation of narcotics or drugs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 831.1. Forfeiture for storage or transportation of narcotics or drugs (2023)
content:
Any wagon, buggy, motor vehicle, water or air craft or other vehicle or conveyance
   in which is stored, contained or transported any narcotics or drugs, the possession
   or transportation of which is in violation of any law of this Commonwealth, shall
   be forfeited to the Commonwealth subject to the provisions hereafter set forth:1Provided, however, That nothing herein contained shall be construed to apply to
   common carriers by railroad subject to Part 1 of the Interstate Commerce Act.2

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Drugs as Evidence›PA ST 35 P.S. § 829. Disposition of confiscated drugs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Drugs as Evidence › PA ST 35 P.S. § 829. Disposition of confiscated drugs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 829. Disposition of confiscated drugs (2023)
content:
The district attorney of the county of this Commonwealth, who shall thus confiscate
   such drugs, is hereby authorized to deliver such drugs to the State Department of
   Health or to any other legally constituted health board of any county of this Commonwealth,
   as in his discretion he may deem fit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Achieving Better Care by Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (Abc-Map) Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.1. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Achieving Better Care by Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (Abc-Map) Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.1. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.1. Short title (2023)
content:
This act shall be known and may be cited as the Achieving Better Care by Monitoring
   All Prescriptions Program (ABC-MAP) Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Achieving Better Care by Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (Abc-Map) Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.2. Purpose
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Achieving Better Care by Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (Abc-Map) Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.2. Purpose
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.2. Purpose (2023)
content:
This act is intended to increase the quality of patient care by giving prescribers
   and dispensers access to a patient's prescription medication history through an electronic
   system that will alert medical professionals to potential dangers for purposes of
   making treatment determinations.  The act further intends that patients will have a thorough and easily obtainable
   record of their prescriptions for purposes of making educated and thoughtful health
   care decisions.  Additionally, the act seeks to aid regulatory and law enforcement agencies in the
   detection and prevention of fraud, drug abuse and the criminal diversion of controlled
   substances.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Achieving Better Care by Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (Abc-Map) Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.6. Establishment of program

      procurement and other support services as directed by the board.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Achieving Better Care by Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (Abc-Map) Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.7. Requirements for dispensers and pharmacies

      submit information to the system regarding each controlled substance dispensed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Achieving Better Care by Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (Abc-Map) Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.9. Access to prescription information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Achieving Better Care by Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (Abc-Map) Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.9. Access to prescription information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.9. Access to prescription information (2023)

      and records of requests to query the system shall be confidential and not subject
      to disclosure under the act of February 14, 2008 (P.L. 6, No. 3),1known as the Right-to-Know Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Achieving Better Care by Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (Abc-Map) Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 872.11. Program funding

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Safe Emergency Prescribing Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 873.4. Referral to treatment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Safe Emergency Prescribing Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 873.4. Referral to treatment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 873.4. Referral to treatment (2023)
content:
A health care practitioner shall refer an individual for treatment if the individual
   is believed to be at risk for substance abuse while seeking treatment in an emergency

   by another health care practitioner, the prescribing health care practitioner shall
   query the prescription drug monitoring program in accordance with section 8 of the
   act of October 27, 2014 (P.L. 2911, No. 191),1known as the Achieving Better Care By Monitoring All Prescriptions Program (ABC-MAP)

   of treatment while undergoing care in an emergency department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Caustic Acids, Alkalies and Mineral Salts›PA ST 35 P.S. § 932. “Caustic” defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Caustic Acids, Alkalies and Mineral Salts › PA ST 35 P.S. § 932. “Caustic” defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 932. “Caustic” defined (2023)
content:
The word“caustic”shall, within the intent and purpose of this act, be construed to mean any acids
   or alkalies in liquid or powdered form, or preparations thereof, on containing free
   or chemically unneutralized hydrochloric acid in a concentration of ten (10) per centum,
   or sulphuric acid in a concentration of ten (10) per centum, or nitric acid in a concentration
   of five (5) per centum, or carbolic acid (phenol) in a concentration of five (5) per
   centum or oxalic acid in a concentration of ten (10) per centum, or acetic acid in
   a concentration of twenty (20) per centum, or hypochlorous acid (calx chlorinata,
   bleaching powder, or chloride of lime) in a concentration of one hundred per centum
   (100), or potassium hydrate (caustic potash, Vienna paste, pearlash, potassa carbonas)
   in a concentration of ten (10) per centum, or sodium hydrate (caustic soda, concentrated
   lye) in a concentration of twenty (20) per centum, or silver nitrate (lunar caustic)
   in a concentration of five (5) per centum.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Generic Equivalent Drug Law›PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.4. Posting requirements; price lists
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Generic Equivalent Drug Law › PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.4. Posting requirements; price lists
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.4. Posting requirements; price lists (2023)
content:
(a) Every pharmacy shall post in a prominent place that is in clear and unobstructed
      public view, at or near the place where prescriptions are dispensed, a sign which
      shall read:  “Pennsylvania law permits pharmacists to substitute a less expensive
      generically equivalent drug or interchangeable biological product for a brand name
      drug unless you or your physician direct otherwise.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Generic Equivalent Drug Law›PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.3. Substitutions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Generic Equivalent Drug Law › PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.3. Substitutions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.3. Substitutions (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever a pharmacist receives a prescription for a brand name drug, the pharmacist
      shall substitute a less expensive generically equivalent drug unless requested otherwise
      by the purchaser or indicated otherwise by the prescriber.  The bottom of every prescription blank shall be imprinted with the words “substitution
      permissible” and shall contain one signature line for the physician's or other authorized
      prescriber's signature.  The prescriber's signature shall validate the prescription and, unless the prescriber
      handwrites “brand necessary” or “brand medically necessary,” shall designate approval
      of substitution of a drug by a pharmacist pursuant to this act.  Imprinted conspicuously on the prescription blanks shall be the words:  “In order
      for a brand name product to be dispensed, the prescriber must handwrite ‘brand necessary’
      or ‘brand medically necessary’ in the space below.”  All information printed on the prescription blank shall be in eight-point uppercase
      print.  In the case of an oral prescription, there will be no substitution if the prescriber
      expressly indicates to the pharmacist that the brand name drug is necessary and substitution
      is not allowed.  Substitution of a less expensive generically equivalent drug shall be contingent
      on whether the pharmacy has the brand name or generically equivalent drug in stock.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Generic Equivalent Drug Law›PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.1. Purpose of act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Generic Equivalent Drug Law › PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.1. Purpose of act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.1. Purpose of act (2023)
content:
It is the purpose of this act to permit consumers to secure necessary drugs at the
   most economical cost consistent with the professional discretion of the purchaser's
   physician and pharmacist.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Caustic Acids, Alkalies and Mineral Salts›PA ST 35 P.S. § 931. Regulation of sale; labels
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Caustic Acids, Alkalies and Mineral Salts › PA ST 35 P.S. § 931. Regulation of sale; labels
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 931. Regulation of sale; labels (2023)
content:
On and after the first day of January, one thousand nine hundred and twenty-four,
   it is unlawful for any person or copartnership or corporation to sell, at wholesale
   or retail, within this Commonwealth, any caustic acids or caustic alkalies, or preparations
   containing such acids or alkalies, intended for household use, or mineral or chemical
   salts for agricultural purposes, without affixing to the bottle, box, vessel, sack,
   or package containing the same, a label printed or plainly written, containing the
   name of the article, the name and place of business of the manufacturer, seller, or
   distributor of such household acids, alkalies, or preparations thereof, and in addition
   the word “Poison,” which shall conspicuously appear thereon in capital letters, not
   less than twenty-four point size, or which shall be affixed thereto as a sticker conspicuously
   placed:  Provided, That in the case of mineral or chemical salts, including nitrate
   of soda, sulphate of ammonia, muriate of potash, sulphate of potash, intended or sold
   for agricultural purposes, the sacks, packages, or other containers, or attached cards
   or labels, shall have printed thereon, as hereinbefore provided, the words “Poisonous
   to live stock.”

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Overdose Mapping Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.27. Funding
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Overdose Mapping Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.27. Funding
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.27. Funding (2023)
content:
(a) Federal funds.--The Pennsylvania State Police shall pursue any available Federal funding to implement,

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Overdose Mapping Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.25. Implementation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety › Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances › Overdose Mapping Act › PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.25. Implementation

content:
(a) Limitation of liability.--Authorized users who report information about an overdose under this act in good faith
      are immune from civil liability or damages for making the report, unless their acts
      or omissions constitute willful and wanton misconduct.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 35 P.S. Health and Safety›Chapter 6B. Drugs, Poisons and Dangerous Substances›Overdose Mapping Act›PA ST 35 P.S. § 960.24. Entry requirements for law enforcement

content:

      the overdose information network to report and document the incident in accordance
      with subsection (b) within 72 hours of the overdose.
